note: Engineering draft. Every action is a conversation or tracking step. None names a medicine, supplement, dose or diet plan. Each needs clinical review before release.

actions.title: Understand your risk
actions.detail: Ask your doctor what your predicted {raised} risk means for you.

actions.title: Ask about the difference
actions.detail: Ask your doctor why your blood results and your predicted risk point in different directions.

actions.title: Keep track of changes
actions.detail: Repeat the relevant tests if your doctor advises.

actions.title: Keep it this way
actions.detail: Keep up the habits that are working for you.

story_actions.title: Add gentle movement to your day
story_actions.what: Build up daily movement slowly, for example a short brisk walk, and add a little more each week.
story_actions.why: You have reported low physical activity, and regular activity supports healthier cholesterol patterns and heart health.
story_actions.safety_note: If you have chest pain, breathlessness or a medical condition, check with your doctor before increasing activity.
story_actions.condition_note: You have reported a health condition. Check with your doctor before increasing your activity.

story_actions.title: Keep up your activity
story_actions.what: Keep up the regular activity you have reported. Whether your routine needs to change is a good question for your doctor.
story_actions.why: You have reported being active, so basic advice to start moving does not apply. Other things can influence these results.

story_actions.title: Tell your doctor how active you are
story_actions.what: Describe how active you are in a usual week when you speak to your doctor.
story_actions.why: Your activity level is not clearly recorded, and it can influence cholesterol and heart health.

story_actions.title: Add fibre rich foods
story_actions.what: Include more of foods such as oats, beans, lentils, chickpeas, fruit, vegetables, nuts and seeds, in ways that suit your own diet.
story_actions.why: Your LDL related cholesterol is outside the laboratory range, and fibre rich plant foods are generally linked with healthier cholesterol.
story_actions.what_without_nuts: Include more of foods such as oats, beans, lentils, chickpeas, fruit and vegetables, in ways that suit your own diet and allergies.

story_actions.title: Add fibre rich foods and healthier protein
story_actions.what: Include more oats, beans, lentils, fruit, vegetables, nuts and seeds. When you eat non vegetarian food, fish can replace some fried or processed meat.
story_actions.why: Your LDL related cholesterol is outside the laboratory range, and fibre rich foods and healthier protein choices are generally linked with healthier cholesterol.
story_actions.what_without_nuts: Include more oats, beans, lentils, fruit and vegetables. When you eat non vegetarian food, fish can replace some fried or processed meat.

story_actions.title: Choose healthier fats
story_actions.what: Choose nuts, seeds and plant oils more often than fried and packaged foods.
story_actions.why: The type of fat in your diet can influence your cholesterol results.
story_actions.safety_note: If you have a nut allergy, choose seeds or other foods that are safe for you.
story_actions.what_without_nuts: Choose plant oils such as olive or mustard oil more often than fried and packaged foods, in ways that suit your allergies.

story_actions.title: Cut back on sugar and alcohol
story_actions.what: Have fewer sugary drinks and sweets, and limit alcohol if you drink.
story_actions.why: Your triglycerides are outside the laboratory range, and sugar and alcohol are known to influence triglycerides.

story_actions.title: Have your blood pressure checked
story_actions.what: Ask for a blood pressure reading if you have not had one recently.
story_actions.why: Your blood report does not measure blood pressure, and it is an important part of heart health.

story_actions.title: Discuss your results with your doctor
story_actions.what: Share these results and your Bio-AI assessment with your doctor and ask what they mean for you.
story_actions.why: Your doctor can look at your results together with your history, which this app cannot do.

story_actions.title: Keep up what is working
story_actions.what: Keep up the habits that support your heart, such as regular movement and a balanced diet.
story_actions.why: Your heart related results and assessment are not raised. That does not mean you are risk free, so regular checkups still matter.
